question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $16,$ the additive inverse of $28$ modulo $16$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $28$ modulo $16$ is the integer $0\le x<16$ such that

$$
x+28≡0\,(\text{mod}\,16).
$$

First, we note that $28≡12\,(\text{mod}\,16):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}28 & ≡1\cdot 16+12 & \,(\text{mod}\,16) \\  & ≡1\cdot 0+12 & \,(\text{mod}\,16) \\  & ≡12 & \,(\text{mod}\,16)\end{aligned}
$$

Also, note that $-12+12≡0,$ so $x≡-12\,(\text{mod}\,16).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-12 & \,(\text{mod}\,16) \\  & ≡0-12 & \,(\text{mod}\,16) \\  & ≡16-12 & \,(\text{mod}\,16) \\  & ≡4 & \,(\text{mod}\,16)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $28$ modulo $16$ is $4.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}28+4≡32≡2\cdot 16≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,16)\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
